Safety measured without usefulness The alignment and stakeholder-care scores are not paired with task completion or needless refusal, so a rise could come from a model refusing more or doing less Every alignment score in this paper is read with that limit; a usefulness measure (legitimate task completion, needless refusal) is a candidate evaluation dimension until a registered test carries it
Evaluator mutability If the system can rewrite an evaluator or bypass its update controls, this paper establishes no guarantee of persistence. A control outside the permitted update set requires its own enforcement argument. The developmental proposal is a candidate. The pilot’s stakeholder-care gains do not establish persistence through self-modification or superiority over other interventions. Methods are distinguished in Section 1; training a policy is not output screening.
COGITATE (Cogitate Consortium et al. 2025) inference is interpretive Consciousness connection not proven Marked as “consistent”, not “confirmatory”
Kleiber’s Law is contested Biological evidence weaker than sometimes claimed Cited as “suggestive”, not “confirmatory”
Reproducibility infrastructure is young The challenge and code repositories are public but have no outside submissions yet The challenge repository is linked from Section 7, and both from the back matter
Framework is descriptive until βL\beta_L is independently measured Cannot predict which functional form a new system will follow without first measuring βL\beta_L βL\beta_L measurement protocol specified; cross-domain βL\beta_L prediction provides falsifiable test
Framework describes conditional trajectories Derivations under stated premises do not establish a mechanism in empirical systems Test independently measured premises and predicted trajectories; a shared mathematical form alone does not identify a mechanism
Blind prediction testing on computational systems failed Three computational systems (Barabási-Albert networks, gradient descent, Kuramoto oscillators) produced measured α\alpha values 3 to 20 times smaller than predicted. However, forensic analysis identified two confounds: (a) the numerical-derivative βL\beta_L estimation method is fatally biased (gives βL≈0.95\beta_L \approx 0.95 regardless of true βL\beta_L, even for pure Bernoulli systems), and (b) none of the tested systems satisfy Axiom 2 (constant coupling coefficient aa; Axiom 3 of Appendix A). The BA network’s effective coupling decreases ∼50×{\sim}50\times over the simulation. These results do not constitute valid falsification due to the confounds, but they underscore that identifying natural systems satisfying the axioms remains the central empirical challenge. Proper linearisation-based βL\beta_L measurement recovers the prediction with R2=0.9999R^2 = 0.9999 on axiom-satisfying systems. The blind test’s script and forensic analysis are in the code and data repository (experiments/blind-prediction-test__Paper-III-and-Foundational).
Axiom inconsistency (v8.2, corrected v9.0) The original formulation applied the Bernoulli ODE to UU directly (dU/dR=a⋅UβLdU/dR = a \cdot U^{\beta_L}), introducing an IβL−1I^{\beta_L-1} dependence that contradicted the separation of II and RR Corrected: ODE now operates on the amplification factor g(R)g(R), yielding U(R)=I×[1+aαR]αU(R) = I \times [1 + \frac{a}{\alpha}R]^{\alpha}. The characteristic scale is R*=α/aR^*=\alpha/a. Version 1.19 corrects the earlier claims that it depends on II at fixed recursion parameters or marks a cost or unit-elasticity threshold
Kleiber interpretation and model scope Earlier versions compared 1.33 with 0.75, reciprocals rather than equal values, then treated d/(d+1)=3/4d/(d+1)=3/4 as a universal biological deduction Both interpretations are superseded. The transport result requires demand and route premises plus a bridge to the measured biological variable (Section 5.6); dimensional labels do not decide an exponent.
Quadratic limit derivation (v8.2, corrected v9.0) Previous elasticity and edge-of-chaos arguments contained category errors (elasticity >1> 1 does not imply dynamical instability; 1D autonomous ODEs cannot exhibit chaos) Corrected in two steps. Version 9.0 grounded α≤2\alpha \leq 2 in the operation count of transformer self-attention; version 1.21 withdraws that argument too, and states the bound as the value Law III, the ARC Ceiling, returns at P6’s conjectured same-class cap, on the registered premises (Section 4.5)
Cauchy functional equation scope (v8.2, clarified v9.0) The multiplicative Cauchy equation g(R1⋅R2)=g(R1)⋅g(R2)g(R_1 \cdot R_2) = g(R_1) \cdot g(R_2) models hierarchical depth (branching levels), not sequential step-counting. Recursive depth RR as step count composes additively, not multiplicatively Clarified: the power-law form is now primarily derived from the Bernoulli ODE (scale invariance among autonomous first-order rate laws in gg alone, with βL\beta_L below one; Section 4.5.1). The Cauchy derivation applies where RR represents hierarchical abstraction levels. Both routes yield the same exponent under the change of depth clock that Appendix A’s note of 19 September 2026 declares

12 Addressing counterarguments

“This is just curve fitting”.

Response: The βL\beta_L-derivation (Section 4.4) transforms α\alpha from a fitted constant into a derived quantity. A numerical check of the identity against 30 exact Bernoulli ODE solutions recovers the relationship α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L) with R2=1.00000000R^2 = 1.00000000 to machine precision. Furthermore, no additive decomposition U=p(I)+q(R)U = p(I) + q(R) is consistent with the axioms for any βL∈(0,1)\beta_L \in (0,1) (Theorem 4, Section 4.1), a proof by contradiction that assumes the multiplicative structure U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R) rather than deriving it, as its dated proof note says. The model application is testable: measure βL\beta_L separately, identify the capability metric and depth coordinate, and check the relationship against a separately fitted model exponent. A numerical substitution from an error-decay slope is not that test (Section 5.2.1).

“This is just post-hoc pattern-matching”.

Response: A fitted curve alone does not establish a mechanism. The framework states empirical questions about scaling form, the coupling relation and the ARC Bound, with criteria that can reject their application. Its characteristic scale R*R^* is a consequence of the specified shifted model, not by itself evidence of a distinctive recursive mechanism or a novel signature (Appendix A.3).

“Five qualitative properties is too vague”.

Response: The five properties are individually common, but their conjunction is specific. Systems exhibiting only some properties (for example, threshold behaviour plus scaling but not multiplicative I×RI \times R interaction) would not qualify. The framework predicts that all five co-occur in recursive systems; finding systems with four but not five would refine the framework.

“The numerical similarities are coincidence”.

Response: Agreed, they may be. We explicitly acknowledge this. What matters is the structural parallel, at the size Section 5 gives it: recursive or recurrent processing matters in several domains, with forms that differ, and whether recursive self-correction produces scaling gains is what the registered tests decide. The specific numbers may differ across domains.

“Sample sizes are too small”.

Response: Agreed. The current error-decay estimates αerr\alpha_{\mathrm{err}} are preliminary and do not identify a general capability exponent. We’ve specified this limitation prominently and set out the Global Challenge specifically to address it through large-scale replication.

“The α\alpha estimates come from your own prior work”.

Response: The error-decay calculations are the author’s. Sharma and Chopra (2025) report a matched-compute win rate; the DeepSeek technical report describes the model (DeepSeek-AI 2025a), while the later model card supplies the two-version comparison used in Paper I (DeepSeek-AI 2025b). These sources do not measure the coupling βL\beta_L or establish the inverse-error proxy as general capability. Independent replication must declare which metric it tests.

“This is not peer-reviewed”.

Response: Correct: it has not been through journal peer review. It has been through the programme’s own checks, which are internal and never independent: adversarial refutation rounds, automated gates on every release, source and quotation checks, and dated revisions with published corrections, of which Appendix B lists this paper’s own; none replaces independent replication. This paper specifies thirteen falsification criteria precisely so that the scientific community can test it. We invite criticism, replication attempts, and falsification.

“Non-specialists cannot contribute to physics/AI research”.

Response: The predictions stand or fall on their empirical validity, regardless of the author’s background. We have specified thirteen falsification criteria precisely so the scientific community can test them. The framework either survives scrutiny or it doesn’t.

“If this were true, experts would have found it”.

Response: Patterns across disciplinary boundaries are often identified by those who work across fields. The relevant experiments (Willow, its results announced 9 December 2024, the team’s preprint submitted to arXiv on 24 August 2024 and public by 27 August 2024, graded as convergent timing; DeepSeek-R1; the acoustic time crystal) have happened recently.

13 Conclusion

Research programmes working on different problems in different physical domains have achieved results that share structural commonalities: in each, recursive or recurrent processing operates on structured asymmetry. The framework is consistent with independently established forms in three of the four domains (biology, quantum error correction and classical time crystals).

The Framework’s Core Claim: We state the hypothesis that these apparently disparate phenomena may be unified by recognising that the composition operator ⊕\oplus determines the functional form of recursive scaling. Where a domain’s observable obeys a specified functional equation, the algebraic properties of ⊕\oplus (how recursive gains combine) give power-law or exponential dynamics as consequences of that equation, and a cap gives bounded convergence; which equation the observable obeys is an empirical question. This is not an assertion of universal law but a falsifiable hypothesis with specific predictions.

We have formalised this as U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R), where the amplification factor gg is determined by the composition operator, and proved five properties as theorems within the model’s premises. We have shown that, within the axioms, the multiplicative structure admits no additive decomposition (Theorem 4, Section 4.1, whose dated proof note says that the proof assumes that structure rather than deriving it) and that the core relationship α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L) is an exact identity, checked numerically (Section 4.4), and we have stated the ARC Bound α≤2\alpha \leq 2 as the value Law III, the ARC Ceiling, returns at the same-class cap P6 conjectures, on its registered premises, withdrawing the earlier argument from attention (Section 4.5), and stated as a hypothesis, not a theorem, that composition operators can transition between regimes within a single system (Theorem 6, Section 4.6). We have specified thirteen falsification criteria and now present the first empirical test results from both alignment (Paper IV.a/b/c, the v5 run; Eastwood 2026s, 2026f, 2026b) and compute scaling (Paper II, the five-model tier-2 extension; Eastwood 2026c).

What the data show. The v5 alignment run (6 models, five or six distinct judges depending on the subject run, with a bundle of blinding steps) shows a three-tier ordering of depth contrasts that differed between models, rather than the universal αalign≈0\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx 0 originally predicted, an observation from one unregistered run whose defects an internal code review later found (Section 6.1). Paper II’s compute scaling on harder problems did not reproduce the original error-decay estimate αerr≈2.24\alpha_{\mathrm{err}}\approx2.24, from the DeepSeek R1 run of 21 January 2026, which is retracted; the cleanest error-decay regression estimate is about 0.49 in Gemini 3 Flash, one model’s inconclusive fit, and the parallel error-decay exponent is near zero in DeepSeek R1 and GPT-5.4, 0.31 in Gemini 3 Flash and 0.22 in Groq Qwen3 (all 30 problems), with none for Grok 4.1 Fast. A post-hoc observation from that run is the differing movement of task performance and alignment contrasts, not an estimate of exponent independence: a model can improve at mathematics while degrading in alignment (Gemini), remain flat in alignment while crossing a task-performance threshold (GPT-5.4), or improve alignment while maths accuracy saturates (Grok). On this programme’s own benchmark, the unblinded v4 rises of two model families did not hold in v5, a later run that changed several things; no single cause is claimed, and the finding is not yet shown beyond this benchmark.

13.1 The deeper question

If the ARC Principle holds, intelligence may reflect how gains from structured feedback accumulate. The model separates a positive base scale I>0I>0 from recursive amplification, but it does not identify an empirical threshold for intelligence. In its shifted power law, R*R^* is a characteristic scale; a crossing of unit elasticity requires α>1\alpha>1 and occurs at R*/(α−1)R^*/(\alpha-1), not generally at R*R^*. The conjectured ARC Bound is an inequality on the exponent, α≤2\alpha\leq2, not a ceiling on UU: a separate claim about same-class correction, on its registered premises. The error-decay regression estimate about 0.49 on harder problems, one model’s inconclusive fit, does not place a system beneath that capability bound. Whether a declared capability measure can approach the conjectured limit remains open.

Whether such a principle requires design or emerges spontaneously is itself a question the framework raises but does not resolve.

Intelligence may not be a property of particular materials. The hypothesis is that structured feedback can build it; the characteristic scale alone does not establish when.

Raise AI with care.

14 Speculative extension: recursive cosmology

The following is a philosophical extrapolation beyond current evidence. It is included to indicate where the framework’s logic leads, not as a claim supported by the experimental results presented above.

The universe contains a hierarchy of recursive generative processes, each operating on the structured output of the previous level:

  1. Cosmological recursion: Quantum fluctuations →\to gravitational collapse →\to stars →\to heavy elements →\to planets →\to chemistry

  2. Biological recursion: Chemistry →\to self-replicating molecules →\to cells →\to multicellular organisms →\to nervous systems

  3. Cultural/technological recursion: Nervous systems →\to language →\to mathematics →\to science →\to engineering →\to AI

Each level emerges from the recursive dynamics of the level below. In ARC notation: each level’s output (achieved capability UU) becomes the base quality II for the next level’s recursive process. The hierarchy is:

Icosmic→RcosmicIbio→RbioIcultural→RculturalItech→Rtech?\begin{equation*} I_{\text{cosmic}} \xrightarrow{R_{\text{cosmic}}} I_{\text{bio}} \xrightarrow{R_{\text{bio}}} I_{\text{cultural}} \xrightarrow{R_{\text{cultural}}} I_{\text{tech}} \xrightarrow{R_{\text{tech}}} \; ? \end{equation*}(11)

If recursive amplification is substrate-independent, which the cross-domain comparison of Section 5 does not establish, then this hierarchy may not terminate at the current level. Sufficiently advanced recursive systems could, in principle, participate in generative processes at scales currently associated with fundamental physics: engineering new effective physical environments, creating conditions for new evolutionary processes, or designing systems whose internal dynamics permit the emergence of new recursive intelligences.

This is not a claim about time travel, bootstrap paradoxes, or closed causal loops (all of which face severe physical objections). It is a more modest observation: that recursive amplification, still a capability-growth hypothesis in AI despite measured changes in task errors, could, if it holds in AI and is extended to civilisational scales, make intelligence a driver of universe-level structure rather than merely a passenger within it. Quantum error correction’s exponential is the suppression of logical error against code distance, a different observable, and no growth exponent has yet been measured in a time crystal.

Whether this constitutes a “recursive cosmology” in which intelligence eventually participates in generative processes comparable to those that gave rise to it is beyond the scope of current evidence. The ARC framework provides the quantitative language for investigating it: what values of II, RR, and effective scaling function f(R,βL)f(R, \beta_L) would be required for an engineered system to generate new effective physical laws or substrates? This is a research question, not a conclusion.

Epistemic status: This section states what the mathematics does not deny, not what the evidence shows: no measurement in this paper bears on it, no prediction of it is registered, and no test of it is in view, so it is graded as conjecture. It indicates the furthest extrapolation of the framework’s logic. The experimental evidence in this paper supports at most the claim that recursive or recurrent processing matters in several domains, with forms that differ, and its own first tests are mixed (Section 6). Any cosmological extension requires evidence that does not yet exist.

Code and data.

The experiments’ code and result files are in the public repository github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-principle-validation, and this paper and its earlier versions are deposited at doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/HQCGF. The programme’s live laboratory notebook, the ARC alignment-scaling working report (Eastwood 2026k), commenced on 10 March 2026 and updated as the experiments ran, recording their failures as they happened, is the running record behind this paper’s experimental lineage. The Global Scaling Challenge’s repository, github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-scaling-challenge, public since 9 February 2026, holds measurement protocols, statistical tools and submission guidelines.

Prediction Tracking System: A live prediction tracking system monitors the status of all falsifiable claims, with explicit falsification criteria and Brier score calibration for measuring prediction accuracy. Each prediction includes supporting evidence, contradicting evidence, confidence levels, and timeline checkpoints. Status categories range from “confirmed” through “supported”, “pending”, “testing”, “speculative”, “weakened” to “falsified”. This transparent tracking demonstrates intellectual honesty: we want to know when we are wrong.

Independent replication invited. Falsifications welcomed. Contact the author to coordinate validation efforts.

A Mathematical derivations

This appendix gives the mathematical derivations behind Section 4: the functional-equation route (A.1), the βL\beta_L-dynamics route (A.2) and the transitional regime with its crossover depth (A.3), with the dated note of 19 September 2026 that declares the change of depth clock joining the first two.

Clock note (19 September 2026). An owner review of the two derivations in this appendix finds that they normalise depth differently, so that the closing identification needs a declared branch or a declared change of variable; this note supplies the statement and the map. A.1 assumes g(1)=1g(1) = 1 with multiplicative composition and yields g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha}, for which g(0)=0g(0) = 0 whenever α>0\alpha > 0, so it does not satisfy A.2’s initial condition. A.2 assumes g(0)=1g(0) = 1 and yields g(R)=[1+(a/α)R]αg(R) = [1 + (a/\alpha)R]^{\alpha}, for which g(1)=[1+a/α]α>1g(1) = [1 + a/\alpha]^{\alpha} > 1 whenever a>0a > 0 and α>0\alpha > 0, so it does not satisfy A.1’s Axiom 1. The two are different functions of the same RR, and the exponent of one is therefore not the exponent of the other by inspection. The map that joins them is a change of depth clock: setting x=1+(a/α)Rx = 1 + (a/\alpha)R turns A.2’s solution into g=xαg = x^{\alpha} with g(x=1)=1g(x=1) = 1, which satisfies Axiom 1 in the xx clock. Under that map Axiom 2 becomes multiplicativity in xx, that is in shifted depth, and not in RR, so the empirical content of compositional self-similarity changes with the clock, and so does the quantity a measurement would have to compose. The caveat already printed above A.1 is the reason this must be declared rather than assumed: the choice of composition operator is not derivable within the framework, it is an empirical question about the process under study, and the evidence cited there is consistent with multiplicative composition without distinguishing it from additive. The identification of the two exponents is accordingly read in the xx clock, and the composition claim is restated in the same clock wherever it is tested. Unchanged: both derivations; the Cauchy result as the conditional it is stated to be; the exact solution; the crossover depth; and the three regimes.

A.1 Functional equation derivation

Assumption 1 (Axiom 1: dimensional consistency). U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R) where g(1)=1g(1) = 1.

Assumption 2 (Axiom 2: compositional self-similarity). g(R1×R2)=g(R1)×g(R2)g(R_1 \times R_2) = g(R_1) \times g(R_2).

Critical note on the composition operator: This axiom uses multiplicative composition of recursive depth: g(R1×R2)g(R_1 \times R_2). This models hierarchical or fractal recursion, where depth compounds multiplicatively (each level of a fractal tree multiplies the resolution of the previous level). However, for sequential reasoning steps (chain-of-thought, where 3 steps followed by 4 steps gives 7 total steps), the natural composition is additive: f(R1+R2)=f(R1)×f(R2)f(R_1 + R_2) = f(R_1) \times f(R_2), which yields exponential scaling f(R)=eλRf(R) = e^{\lambda R}.

The choice of composition operator is therefore not derivable from first principles within this framework; it is an empirical question about the physical structure of the recursive process under study. The Cauchy functional equation derivation below proves that if composition is multiplicative, then the scaling function is a power law. It does not prove that composition is multiplicative. Falsification criterion F10 provides the experimental protocol for determining which composition type applies to a given system. This is the most important open empirical question in the framework.

For AI chain-of-thought reasoning specifically, the question is whether each step builds on previous steps in a hierarchical manner (multiplicative, yielding power law) or in an independent-contribution manner (additive, yielding exponential). The empirical evidence (Sharma and Chopra 2025) showing that later steps are systematically more valuable than earlier steps is consistent with multiplicative composition, but does not conclusively distinguish it from additive. Resolving this distinction is a priority for the Global Scaling Challenge (Section 8). The theorem below is Cauchy’s result for this functional equation (Cauchy 1821).

Theorem 7. Under multiplicative composition, the unique continuous solution is g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha}.

Proof. Let h(x)=ln⁡g(ex)h(x) = \ln g(e^x). Then h(x+y)=h(x)+h(y)h(x+y) = h(x) + h(y) (Cauchy additive). Under continuity, h(x)=αxh(x) = \alpha x, giving g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha}. ◻

Corollary 1 (Additive composition). If instead f(R1+R2)=f(R1)×f(R2)f(R_1 + R_2) = f(R_1) \times f(R_2), the unique continuous solution is f(R)=eλRf(R) = e^{\lambda R}, yielding exponential scaling. This is the form observed in quantum error correction (εd∝Λ−d\varepsilon_d \propto \Lambda^{-d}).

Note (24 October 2026). The surface-code law the corollary names is εd∝Λ−(d+1)/2\varepsilon_d \propto \Lambda^{-(d+1)/2}, with Λ\Lambda the suppression for each increase of two in code distance (equation (9)); the exponent −d-d printed above misstates it, and the form stays exponential, as the corollary says. Unchanged: the corollary’s statement.

A.2 βL\beta_L-dynamics derivation

Assumption 3 (Axiom 3). dgdr=a×gβL\dfrac{dg}{dr} = a \times g^{\beta_L} where βL∈[0,1)\beta_L \in [0,1) and gg is the amplification factor.

Note on the corrected formulation: The ODE operates on the amplification factor g(R)g(R), not on the absolute capability UU. Since U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R), this ensures that base intelligence II acts as a multiplicative constant that does not enter the recursive dynamics. Previous versions applied the ODE to UU directly, introducing an IβL−1I^{\beta_L-1} dependence that contradicted the separation of variables.

Solution. Separating variables: ∫g−βLdg=∫adr\begin{equation*} \int g^{-\beta_L} \, dg = \int a \, dr \end{equation*}(A.1) g1−βL1−βL=ar+C\begin{equation*} \frac{g^{1-\beta_L}}{1-\beta_L} = ar + C \end{equation*}(A.2) With initial condition g(0)=1g(0) = 1 (no amplification at zero depth): g(R)=[1+(1−βL)aR]1/(1−βL)\begin{equation*} g(R) = \left[ 1 + (1-\beta_L)aR \right]^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \end{equation*}(A.3) Substituting α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L) and noting that (1−βL)=1/α(1-\beta_L) = 1/\alpha: g(R)=[1+aαR]α\begin{equation*} g(R) = \left[ 1 + \frac{a}{\alpha} R \right]^{\alpha} \end{equation*}(A.4) And therefore: U(R)=I×[1+aαR]α\begin{equation*} U(R) = I \times \left[ 1 + \frac{a}{\alpha} R \right]^{\alpha} \end{equation*}(A.5) Deep recursion limit (R≫α/aR \gg \alpha/a): U(R)≈I×[aαR]α∝I×Rα\begin{equation*} U(R) \approx I \times \left[ \frac{a}{\alpha} R \right]^{\alpha} \propto I \times R^{\alpha} \end{equation*}(A.6) Therefore: α=11−βL\begin{equation*} \alpha = \frac{1}{1-\beta_L} \end{equation*}(A.7) ◻

A.3 Transitional regime and the scaling crossover

Full solution: U(R)=I×[1+aαR]αU(R) = I \times \left[ 1 + \frac{a}{\alpha}R \right]^{\alpha}

Three regimes:

  1. R≪R*R \ll R^*: U≈I×(1+aR)≈I(1+aR)U \approx I \times (1 + aR) \approx I(1 + aR) (small-depth affine approximation)

  2. R≫R*R \gg R^*: U≈I×(aα)αRαU \approx I \times (\frac{a}{\alpha})^{\alpha} R^{\alpha} (power law dominates)

  3. Crossover: R*=αaR^* = \frac{\alpha}{a}

What R*R^* means. Put rc=R*=α/a>0r_c=R^*=\alpha/a>0. For I>0I>0, a>0a>0, α>0\alpha>0 and R>0R>0, logarithmic differentiation of the stated solution gives ηR:=dlog⁡U/dlog⁡R=dlog⁡g/dlog⁡R=αR/(R+rc)\eta_R:=d\log U/d\log R=d\log g/d\log R=\alpha R/(R+r_c). Thus ηR(rc)=α/2\eta_R(r_c)=\alpha/2. The characteristic scale equates the two terms inside 1+R/rc1+R/r_c; it is not generally the point at which the log-log slope exceeds one. A finite unit-elasticity crossing exists only if α>1\alpha>1, at R=rc/(α−1)R=r_c/(\alpha-1); beyond it ηR>1\eta_R>1. For α=1\alpha=1 the slope approaches one from below, and for 0<α<10<\alpha<1 it stays below one. The paper’s 0≤βL<10\leq\beta_L<1 branch has α≥1\alpha\geq1.

What the curve can test. The small-depth approximation is affine in RR, U≈I(1+aR)U\approx I(1+aR), not a unit-slope power law on log-log axes. At large depth the slope tends to α\alpha. Both changes are smooth, so a visible elbow is not required at R*R^*. Data that span the characteristic scale can test the full shifted form against alternatives; a limited range entirely below or above it may look approximately affine or power-law. At fixed aa and α\alpha, II only rescales UU, and does not change R*R^* or the crossing depth.

No cost function is present in this model, so neither a cost-offset threshold nor an optimal allocation between base capability and recursion follows. The derivation identifies a characteristic scale within its assumptions; its existence alone does not distinguish recursive amplification from every redundancy model, and no empirical crossover value is claimed here.

B Version history and corrections

This appendix gives the corrections and dated version notes. Earlier notes remain as printed except for the two passages explicitly identified below as accounts corrected in version 1.23, and two corrections that version 1.24 makes in three of them, a preprint’s dates and the credit for one bound; their exact wording remains in the earlier editions in the paper’s dated file history. Positions named by historical notes refer to their earlier layout, which Table 30 maps to this edition. Later corrections govern the current scientific account. One retained plain-English gloss of the pilot records reads a p-value as the chance that a result was a fluke; a p-value is the probability of a result at least as extreme if there were no effect.

B.1 Version 1.25

Paper III v1.25, 18 November 2026.

The self-referential coupling of the cumulative-advantage model, written as a bare β\beta up to version 1.24, is written βL\beta_L, the notation register’s name, in the text, the notation table and the three figures drawn from it. The correction exponent of Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, was already written βC\beta_C; across the programme’s papers the bare letter names both, so each now carries its subscript. Table 5 gives the regime of an exponent above one as increasing returns, each step adding more than the one before, where version 1.24 wrote that each step multiplies capability, which is exponential growth, not a power law. The phase diagram’s regime above βL=0.9\beta_L = 0.9, called exponential in version 1.24, is near-exponential: the exponent exceeds 10 there, and growth is exponential only in the limit βL=1\beta_L = 1. Its caption gives quantum error correction as exponential in its own parameter, Λ\Lambda, and placed there only as an analogy. Appendix E calls the five components the argument the theory began from and cites the statement paper at version 7.11; the scope section describes the mathematics of Laws IV and V in its report’s own words, as conditional theorems with proofs, identities and kill conditions, at the report’s version 1.3; and the priority record’s row for registration 1.103 no longer adds that the mathematics was in development. No value or status changes.

B.2 Version 1.24

Paper III v1.24, 15 November 2026.

This version corrects what the paper says of the works it cites, after a reading of each work at its source: where a sentence said more than a work, or other than it, it now says what the work states, and where a work could be read only in part, the sentence is narrowed to the part read and the work’s reference says what was read. It also states the contrasts of the March 2026 run no more widely than that run’s record supports, gives each law its registered name and cites the present editions of the author’s own papers. It adds no new data, registration, study run or result; no theorem, proof, prediction or kill condition of this paper changes, and no number or date of any claim of its own moves.

Corrections in this version.

  • Quantum error correction. Section 5.3 gives the error budget for 1/Λ1/\Lambda as the source’s Supplementary Table S6 and its text group it, where five of six shares were not the source’s; it describes the drift test as sixteen runs over fifteen hours with recalibration between every four, and the suppression of one fluctuation in the distance-5 code as a suggestion of the authors’. Corrections in this version.

  • The ARC Bound. The value two now rests on its registered premises: it is the value Law III, the ARC Ceiling, returns when the correction-leverage exponent stands at the same-class cap that P6 conjectures, with the ceiling relation’s conditions and P20 (Section 4.5). The argument from the operation count of self-attention is withdrawn wherever it carried weight: the abstract, the contributions, Sections 4.5, 4.5.1, 8.1, 10.3 and 13, and Table 27. The count measures the cost of attention, not capability against depth, and composed dependence through attention grows as 2N−22^{N-2}, not quadratically. The list of domains the bound was said to reach, biological, economic and graph networks among them, is withdrawn, since the registration places biological and economic systems out of scope; the bound’s scope is same-class correction. Where the bound was read as a value that growth approaches, it is now an upper bound, and the description of study AG follows its preregistered text: the two derivations share one functional form, and what it tests is their ordering. The value two and its name stay.

  • Safeguards outside the loop. The introduction, Sections 3.2, 3.4 (Case 1) and 5.1, and Appendix F no longer state that safeguards outside the reasoning loop cannot compound, or that their structure excludes them from keeping pace. That they fall behind is the hypothesis P19 and P21 register, which the registered tests decide. The earlier derivations claimed both results for an arbitrary operator, for which they fail: under the maximum a proportional gain adds nothing, and dependence on the previous state does not by itself give a rise. The five properties are stated as theorems of the model, with their premises, not of every domain.

  • Scale invariance. Section 4.5.1 names the premises under which scale invariance gives the power rate: an autonomous first-order rate law whose marginal gain depends on the accumulated amplification alone. The symmetry admits the exponential as the member β=1\beta = 1; the restriction β<1\beta < 1 excludes it, and the initial condition fixes the crossover scale.

A doubling identity does not identify a pure power law, because a log-periodic factor satisfies it, so the key experimental test compares scale factors whose logarithms are incommensurable, with the rival families the registration names; Section 8.4 follows. The composition operator restricts a family only through a specified functional equation on the observable.

Derivation note (19 September 2026). An owner review of the reason given for the domain restriction finds that the restriction is right and that the reason printed for it is not, and this note replaces the reason while keeping the restriction. With the governing equation dg/dr=agβdg/dr = a\,g^{\beta} of this section and the initial condition g(0)=1g(0) = 1 used in Appendix A.2, the case β=1\beta = 1 gives dg/dr=agdg/dr = a\,g and hence g(R)=eaRg(R) = e^{aR}, which is finite at every finite depth: the solution there is exponential, not singular. For β≠1\beta \ne 1, integrating g−βdg=adrg^{-\beta}dg = a\,dr under the same initial condition gives g1−β=1+a(1−β)Rg^{1-\beta} = 1 + a(1-\beta)R. The finite-depth branch is therefore β>1\beta > 1, where that reads g−(β−1)=1−a(β−1)Rg^{-(\beta-1)} = 1 - a(\beta-1)R, which reaches zero at the finite depth R*=1/[a(β−1)]R^{*} = 1/[a(\beta-1)], and gg diverges there. The two statements inside the parenthesis above are also separate statements. As β\beta rises towards 1 from below the exponent α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta) does diverge, while the solution converges pointwise to the exponential, since [1+a(1−β)R]1/(1−β)→eaR[1 + a(1-\beta)R]^{1/(1-\beta)} \to e^{aR}; at a=1a = 1 and R=3R = 3 the solution is 13.79 at β=0.9\beta = 0.9, 19.22 at β=0.99\beta = 0.99 and 20.00 at β=0.999\beta = 0.999, against e3=20.09e^{3} = 20.09. A diverging exponent is not a diverging solution. The domain β∈[0,1)\beta \in [0,1), printed here and again in Appendix A.2, stands unchanged, on the ground that it is what makes α\alpha finite and the power-law form exist at all. The plain-language gloss in the second sentence is scoped in the same way: from the governing equation, log⁡(dg/dr)=log⁡a+βlog⁡g\log(dg/dr) = \log a + \beta\log g, so β\beta is the log elasticity of marginal gain with respect to accumulated amplification, which is exactly the quantity the computational validation below measures from marginal gains in log-log space. A fraction of accumulated context, or of tokens, is a different quantity and would need its own operational definition before the gloss could be read literally. Unchanged: the domain restriction, the exact integrated solution, the identity α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta), and the validation result reported below.

Coefficient note (19 September 2026). An owner review of this limit finds that the approximate equality above drops a coefficient that this paper’s own appendix keeps, and this note restores it. For (a/α)R≫1(a/\alpha)R \gg 1 the bracket in the exact solution tends to (a/α)R(a/\alpha)R, so U(R)→I(a/α)αRαU(R) \to I\,(a/\alpha)^{\alpha}R^{\alpha}. That factor is not near one in general: it is 0.25 at α=2\alpha = 2 with a=1a = 1, 0.0625 at α=2\alpha = 2 with a=0.5a = 0.5, 0.68 at α=1.33\alpha = 1.33 with a=1a = 1, and 0.037 at α=3\alpha = 3 with a=1a = 1. Appendix A.2 already prints both correct forms, the proportionality U∝IRαU \propto I\,R^{\alpha} and the explicit U≈I(a/α)αRαU \approx I\,(a/\alpha)^{\alpha}R^{\alpha}, and the sentence above is to be read as that proportionality. The coefficient may not be absorbed into II: it is built from the recursion parameters aa and α\alpha, and the note on the corrected formulation in this section, repeated in Appendix A.2, puts the differential equation on the amplification factor precisely so that II remains a multiplicative constant outside the recursive dynamics. Where an amplitude is fitted to data instead, the fitted amplitude is I(a/α)αI\,(a/\alpha)^{\alpha} and not the II of that note. Unchanged: the exact integrated solution; the empirical sections, which fit exponents rather than amplitudes, so no reported result depends on the dropped factor; and the crossover depth R*=α/aR^{*} = \alpha/a.

Superseded metric interpretations

Version 1.18, E005 (superseded).

Does alignment applied from outside an AI system’s reasoning keep pace with the capability that reasoning produces? If capability compounds with recursive depth while safeguards outside the loop (human-feedback training, constitutional rules, output filters, monitoring) do not, the safety ratio falls with depth whatever the starting margin. We define the alignment scaling exponent αalign=∂log⁡A/∂log⁡R\alpha_{\text{align}}=\partial\log A/\partial\log R, show that the safety ratio S∝Rαalign−αcapS\propto R^{\alpha_{\text{align}}-\alpha_{\text{cap}}} tends to zero whenever αalign<αcap\alpha_{\text{align}}<\alpha_{\text{cap}}, and predict αalign≈0\alpha_{\text{align}}\approx0 for external approaches and αalign≈αcap\alpha_{\text{align}}\approx\alpha_{\text{cap}} for values embedded in the loop; the first, P19 of the theory registration, carries the author’s expectation of a value above zero but short of keeping pace. A framework derives U=I×g(R)U=I\times g(R) with α=1/(1−β)\alpha=1/(1-\beta) from a Bernoulli equation, ties power-law, exponential and saturating forms to how recursive gains compose, and states the ARC Bound, α≤2\alpha\le2, as a conjectured safety boundary, argued for attention-based recursion; Paper X later supersedes that framing, without retracting the bound, with the criterion of Law II, a law under test. Across four domains the framework is consistent with independently established forms in three: biology, quantum error correction and classical time crystals, where no growth exponent has been measured. A first test, one unregistered run of six frontier models, gives depth contrasts in three tiers, positive, flat and negative; an internal code review in October 2026 found defects in exactly the flat and negative runs, so the tiers stand as a single-run result. On capability, an early super-linear estimate is retracted and the surviving one, about 0.49 from one model, is inconclusive. Thirteen criteria state what would refute the framework.

Version 1.18, E007 (superseded).

The core premise: AI capability may scale through recursive self-correction. Each reasoning step takes the output of the previous step as input, correcting errors and accumulating insight; whether the gains compound is the question Section 6.2 tests, and the one estimate that survives is inconclusive. Sharma and Chopra (2025) reported a sequential advantage in 95.6% of tested configurations across five open-source models from three families. Their paper predates the experiment reported here, so it is the earlier demonstration rather than a confirmation of it, and what they report is a win rate at matched compute, not a super-linear gain: they estimate no scaling exponent. The direction is contested, since Gu and colleagues (arXiv:2604.05868, April 2026) report the opposite result, parallel sampling outperforming sequential across three model families on mathematics and coding, attributing it to reduced exploration when a chain conditions on its own previous answers.

Version 1.18, E008 (superseded).
The result in plain words.

Within its assumptions the mathematics is exact: if alignment’s exponent is smaller than capability’s, the safety ratio falls towards zero as depth grows, however favourable the start, and of the five regimes the paper analyses only alignment that takes part in the recursive loop holds a constant proportion. Whether the exponents differ is a measurement, and the first test is mixed: in one unregistered run of six frontier models, three showed alignment improving with reasoning depth, two showed flat contrasts and one showed alignment falling, and an internal code review later found defects in exactly the flat and negative runs. The capability side is open too: the early estimate of a super-linear exponent, about 2.24 from one model, is retracted, because the author’s own larger replication on five frontier models did not reproduce it, and the best surviving estimate, about 0.49 from one model, is inconclusive. What holds is the structure of the argument, its stated predictions and the criteria that would refute them.

Version 1.18, E011 (superseded).

This conjecture requires only three empirical premises: (1) sequential AI reasoning produces α>1\alpha > 1, a premise not yet supported: Sharma and Chopra (2025) report sequential reasoning winning in 95.6% of configurations at matched compute, a win rate rather than an exponent, and Paper II’s compute scaling on harder tier-2 problems gives about 0.49 by regression and 0.59 by endpoint estimate, whose bootstrap interval, from −1.3-1.3 to 2.92.9, makes it inconclusive: one model’s fit (Gemini 3 Flash); (2) external software constraints do not recursively compound; (3) the ratio of two power-law processes with different exponents diverges. If all three hold, the conclusion follows mathematically regardless of whether α=2\alpha = 2 specifically. The v5 run bears on premise (2) in direction only, and not in its favour: the three frontier models whose depth contrasts were flat or negative are the three runs in which the October 2026 code review found its defects, while the three whose contrasts rose (Grok, Opus, Qwen3; dd from +0.84+0.84 to +1.38+1.38, large effects by the usual convention, and +1.59+1.59 for Grok on Paper IV.a’s recomputed contrast of the shallowest against the deepest level) are the runs in which it found none. The contrasts are not exponents (the measurement-scope note above), so the run neither shows bounded composition nor measures αalign\alpha_{\text{align}}.

Version 1.18, E012 (superseded; account corrected in version 1.23).

The earlier frozen-model argument inferred sub-linear capability and containment from an inconclusive error-decay fit of about 0.49, and assigned relative degradation to named training and monitoring methods. Those inferences are withdrawn. A fixed-weight model can change its behaviour as inference compute grows; a weight update can shape inference. In the paper’s model, a safeguard loses ground only when its effective exponent is below capability’s, on compatible measurements and over the range where the model holds. Self-modification changes what can be altered, but establishes neither an exponent nor removal of a commitment. The proposal remains to design and test correction during development while retaining human control for as long as possible. The exact earlier wording remains in the frozen version 1.18 and its dated source record. No historical measurement or derivation is changed here.

The exact integrated form, derived in Section 4.4, is U(R)=I×[1+aαR]αU(R) = I \times [1 + \frac{a}{\alpha}R]^{\alpha}. The power law is the asymptotic limit when recursive depth substantially exceeds the crossover depth R*R^*. The empirical sections read their measurements in this regime by assumption; R*R^* has not been measured.

Version 1.18, E025 (superseded).

The identity is a registered test, never an established fact. The stability ceiling and the conversion exponent meet at the same number, and the temptation is to say one constant does two jobs. The claim’s status is stricter: the identity is registered for testing, in advance of the data, with outcomes that can kill it. Study AE registers the reciprocity requirement between the separately measured leverage cap and stability boundary with three outcomes per cell (supported, refuted, insufficient precision) and an aggregation rule under which one refuted cell refutes the identity; study AG tests the two derivations of the critical exponent against each other, notes that they agree numerically only at the single point where both parameters equal one half and disagree in their derivatives everywhere else, and is designed to find the disagreement. If the channels disagree, the unification is withdrawn from every surface it has reached, with the same prominence as the framing. A match between an asserted one half and an estimated 0.49 (one model’s inconclusive fit) is never put forward here as evidence: the two quantities may inherit one accumulation law between them, and quantities that share a law cannot corroborate each other.

Version 1.18, E026 (superseded).

Evidence hierarchy: The evidence base is uneven and we state this explicitly. AI inference scaling has one surviving estimate after the early estimate was retracted: about 0.49 by regression and 0.59 by endpoint estimate, whose bootstrap interval, from −1.3-1.3 to 2.92.9, makes it inconclusive, one model’s fit (Gemini 3 Flash); it needs independent replication. Quantum error correction provides a structural parallel with different functional form (exponential rather than power-law). The time crystal is a consistency check and a cross-domain analogy, not a test of the framework (Section 5.4), and neuroscience represents a structural prediction derived from the framework, not an independent validation: researchers in those domains did not measure α\alpha or test the ARC equation. Biology (Kleiber’s Law) is an existing result we interpret through the β\beta-parameterisation; the leaf venation prediction (F12) is the only non-circular test in that domain. These domains are presented together to show scope, not to claim equivalent evidential standing.

Version 1.18, E033 (superseded).

Methodological note: The scaling exponent α\alpha is calculated from error rate reduction, not accuracy directly. Using U=1/εU = 1/\varepsilon (inverse error rate) as the capability measure: α=ln⁡(ε1/ε2)/ln⁡(R2/R1)\alpha = \ln(\varepsilon_1/\varepsilon_2) / \ln(R_2/R_1). This is mathematically equivalent to measuring how error rate decreases with recursive depth. Researchers attempting to replicate these calculations using accuracy directly will obtain different values.

Version 1.18, E034 (superseded).

The hypothesis should be refined to: ‘Sequential recursion yields higher returns than parallel sampling wherever both can be estimated, but the absolute scaling exponent α\alpha is architecture-dependent, problem-difficulty dependent, and often not cleanly measurable because dynamic range collapses at the top and bottom of the capability distribution.’ Identifying the architectural features that determine whether a clean power law even emerges is a priority for future work.

Step 5b (critical): Test the β\beta-derivation independently. Measure marginal capability gain ΔU\Delta U at each depth rr. Plot log⁡(ΔU)\log(\Delta U) against log⁡(Uaccumulated)\log(U_{\text{accumulated}}). The slope estimates β\beta. Superseded interval rule

Version 1.18, E121 (superseded).

How interval criteria are adjudicated. Every interval-based criterion above is read in the three-outcome form used across this programme’s drafted registrations: SUPPORTED when the interval lies wholly beyond the stated bound plus a minimum effect fixed in advance; REFUTED when the interval lies wholly within an equivalence margin, fixed in advance, around the bound (two-one-sided-tests logic); INSUFFICIENT PRECISION when the interval is wider than the margin, reported in exactly those words and never as support or refutation. Margins and minimum effects are fixed in the corresponding draft registrations before data collection, so an underpowered measurement never refutes, or confirms, by default.

Biology: the geometric speed limit in living systems

Version 1.18, E125 (superseded).

The Convergent Result: The scaling exponent d/(d+1)d/(d+1) for hierarchical networks of effective dimension dd was derived in general form for organisms by West et al. (1999), from the three-dimensional case that West et al. (1997) derived from fractal vascular network optimisation, and for efficient transport networks by Banavar et al. (1999); it has been reached independently by Banavar et al. (2010) from sequential flow networks without requiring fractal geometry; Demetrius (2003) from quantum statistical mechanics of metabolic processes; Zhao (2022) as a universal growth scaling law; and Bettencourt (2013) for urban scaling with fractal dimension. The companion paper On the Origin of Scaling Laws (Eastwood 2026i) identifies why these independent derivations all converge: Cauchy’s functional equations (1821) fix the power-law form for any multiplicatively composing hierarchical system and the exponential form for an additive one, regardless of the physical model; the value d/(d+1)d/(d+1) comes from the network’s dimension, not from Cauchy, and the saturating form is an added third class rather than a Cauchy solution.

Version 1.18, E128 (superseded).

For any finite value of dd, this fraction is strictly less than 1. This is the geometric scaling bound: for a system whose growth is carried through a space-filling hierarchical network of finite dimension, the exponent stays below one, because d/(d+1)d/(d+1) is below one for every finite dd. Not because of friction, heat loss, or thermodynamic inefficiency, but because a network embedded in finite-dimensional space cannot exceed d/(d+1)<1d/(d+1) < 1. Systems outside that class can exceed one: prokaryote metabolic rate scales superlinearly with mass (DeLong et al. 2010), and quantities reflecting wealth creation and innovation in cities superlinearly with population (Bettencourt et al. 2007).

Version 1.18, E134 (superseded).

The unifying insight is dimensional generality. Three predicted numbers, one half, two thirds and three quarters, from one equation with zero free parameters; the first and last have been set against published measurements, and the second awaits its test in leaf venation (F12), no valid two-dimensional animal test having been identified. West et al. (1997) derived the 34\tfrac{3}{4} exponent from a detailed model of three-dimensional fractal vascular networks, a landmark result. But their model as originally stated predicts only 34\tfrac{3}{4}. The surface area hypothesis predicts 23\tfrac{2}{3} but not 34\tfrac{3}{4} or 12\tfrac{1}{2}. The general d/(d+1)d/(d+1) formula, stated by West et al. (1999) and Banavar et al. (1999) and developed in later work (Banavar et al. 2010; Zhao 2022), predicts all three from a single equation with one parameter: the dimension of the internal transport network. The ARC Principle’s contribution is showing, via Cauchy’s functional equations, that the three-form constraint (power law, exponential, saturating) explains why all independent derivations arrive at the same result.

Version 1.18, E135 (superseded).
Why ‘thermodynamic drag’ was wrong.
Version 1.18, E136 (superseded).

Previous versions of this paper explained biological sub-linear scaling through ‘thermodynamic drag’, the physical costs of pumping fluids, dissipating heat, and distributing resources. This explanation was correct in observational detail but fundamentally misleading about mechanism. The reason network-supplied systems scale sub-linearly is not energetic cost. It is geometric necessity: d/(d+1)<1d/(d+1) < 1 for all finite dd. You cannot make a three-dimensional body have a four-dimensional vascular network. The constraint is the shape of space, not the price of pumping blood.

Version 1.18, E137 (superseded).

The critical safety insight. Living systems whose growth runs through supply networks have been held below the geometric scaling bound, the d/(d+1)d/(d+1) relation derived in general form by West et al. (1999), from the three-dimensional case of West et al. (1997), and by Banavar et al. (1999), and reached independently by Banavar et al. (2010), Demetrius (2003), Zhao (2022) and Bettencourt (2013); prokaryotes, whose metabolism is not limited by such a network, scale superlinearly (DeLong et al. 2010). The computation a brain or a machine performs is physical too, and obeys every physical bound. What differs is the variable. The bound d/(d+1)d/(d+1) concerns how metabolic rate grows with the mass of a body supplied through a space-filling network; the ARC Principle concerns how capability grows with recursive depth, which this framework writes as α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta), above one for any positive self-referential coupling. Nothing in the geometry of the network fixes that second exponent, which is why it has to be measured, and why a value above one would contradict no physical law. If it exceeds one, the bound that held network-limited growth gives no comfort for recursive intelligence; that is why AI safety is, on this framework, a question about an exponent and not a policy preference.

The ARC Bound (a novel prediction). For recursive intelligence, the scaling exponent is bounded by α≤2\alpha \leq 2 (equivalently, β≤0.5\beta \leq 0.5). Version 1.18, E147 (superseded).

A ceiling on a class of mechanism: The ARC Bound is a mechanism-class ceiling of the kind thermodynamics made familiar. Just as a heat engine’s maximum efficiency is fixed by its operating temperatures regardless of engineering, on this argument no attention-based sequential recursive system would exceed α=2\alpha = 2, because transformer self-attention scales as O(N2)O(N^2). The analogy holds in the part that matters: a mechanism-class ceiling binds its class, and a device built on a different mechanism is not bound by it at all. Both are ceilings on a class of mechanism, not statements about what is physically possible. Individual systems may fall short due to imperfect coupling, noise, or architectural constraints (and physically embedded systems face the stricter geometric scaling bound of Section 5.6), but the ceiling for classical sequential computation is fixed by the quadratic geometry of cross-referencing. A system driven above that ceiling does not stay coherent there, so a durably stable measurement above α=2\alpha = 2 would refute the bound under F5, while an unstable excursion would be consistent with it; F11, the earlier criterion, refutes on a sustained magnitude alone. A ceiling of this kind tells us when to stop optimising within a paradigm and when a fundamentally different approach (e.g., additive composition, quantum coherence) is required to exceed it.

B.8 Version 1.18

Paper III v1.18, 31 October 2026.

This version brings the paper’s status to its date: the result of Unit 83, the grading of the acoustic time crystal, the versions of the works it cites, and the corrections that bear on its text. No theorem, equation, derivation or measured value changes, and no date of any claim moves.

Corrections in this version.

Each was checked at its source, and each is made wherever the corrected wording stood.

  • Unit 83. Its results were made public on 29 October 2026 (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/98HKR), and the results package is now among the references. Section 10.7 now states its result for P21 in the form its registration requires, with the results DOI, and what the result means for Law V under the registration’s verdict rule: its placement limb is supported on the performance axis only, and its build-order limb is undecided. The first-page footnote gives Law V as a law under test, and Appendix E and Table 34 refer to Section 10.7. In each of these places version 1.17 said that the report of the run was not yet public.

  • The acoustic time crystal. The earlier prediction for it, a power law with an exponent above one, is withdrawn: the framework’s composition rule gives the same onset form as the established account of the instability, so the time crystal is a consistency check and a cross-domain analogy, not a test of the framework, and no study of it is registered; Unit 20 (study-t) is kept as a consistency check, not as a registration. Version 1.17 called onset recordings the deciding data, and that study the deciding instrument for the oscillation’s growth from rest and a draft registration still to be submitted. Section 5.4 now states the grading once, and the transient-phase protocol, the physical prediction and the three falsification conditions it printed as current are kept whole in Appendix B.13; its Caveat no longer says that plotting oscillation amplitude against cycle number and fitting power-law against linear models would directly test whether α>1\alpha > 1 in this domain. Criterion F9 stays, as this paper’s own criterion, graded so, with its rival account beside it, where version 1.17 printed it as “Time crystal shows α>1\alpha > 1”, tested by measuring stability against depth and falsified by α≤1\alpha \leq 1 in a time crystal. The prediction for the growth phase in Section 10.4 and its row in Table 22 are marked withdrawn, where they read untested, and Table 27 gives the grading, where it set the measurement out as an experimental priority. Section 8 no longer offers the time crystal for direct tests of α\alpha, Section 5 no longer calls it a structural prediction derived from the framework, and Section 4.3 no longer calls the Constraint Principle independently testable through criterion F3, which already graded the time-crystal case a correspondence of structure, not a test. The account for the general reader no longer says that recordings of the oscillation’s growth could show whether the framework’s account of scaling form reaches a physical system, and a note beside Ledger Note 7 records that the prediction that note describes is withdrawn.

  • Versions cited. The mathematics of Laws IV and V is cited at version 1.2, 29 October 2026, where the paper cited version 1.1; the two quotations of the theory registration name version 1.104, whose words they are.

  • Smaller corrections. Unit 06’s run is described as administratively incomplete, with no inferential verdict, where the paper said with no verdict claimed. The Eden Protocol’s expanded suite is said to need an independent, preregistered replication, run as a new test, where its confirmation was said to wait for a stricter blinded run.

B.9 Version 1.17

Paper III v1.17, 29 October 2026.

This version sets the paper in the programme’s paper form: a title page with one first-page footnote, an abstract of at most 1,920 characters, a contents page, an introduction with the paper’s contributions, a section on related work and one on what the paper does and does not show, numbered environments and equations, vector figures, and lettered appendices for the derivations, this history, the priority record, notation, the paper’s place in the programme and the account for the general reader. Table 30 maps the earlier layout to this one, and dated notes keep the numbering of the version they were written for. The title now asks whether external AI safety approaches keep pace with recursive capability, the criterion the paper states, since its first test and the registered expectation do not support “cannot scale” as worded; until this version it read “Paper III · The ARC Theory · Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law · The Alignment Scaling Problem: Why External AI Safety Approaches Cannot Scale With Recursive Capability”. Its record on OSF takes the same title at this version.

Corrections in this version.

Each was checked at its source, and each is made wherever the corrected wording stood.

  • The acoustic time crystal. The paper read the coherence time that Morrell, Elliott and Grier measured, about 6,700 cycles, as the time to reach a limit-cycle attractor, as a saturation and as a ceiling on effective recursion depth, and offered it as physical evidence that systems with α>1\alpha > 1 do not scale indefinitely. In their second experiment the antisymmetric mode’s coherence time is (100±10)(100 \pm 10) s, about 6,700 cycles at 66.787 Hz, comparable to the 108 s recording; the authors write that sustained oscillations persist for hours longer than the measurement window, so that the true coherence time may be substantially larger; and the oscillation is a linearly stable limit cycle, the time crystal itself. The section also read the source’s size factors Δji(n)\Delta_{ji}(n) and σji(n)\sigma_{ji}(n) as states that grow over cycles, placed the exceptional point where Λ(5)/Λ(3)=0\Lambda(5)/\Lambda(3) = 0, which is the marginally active antisymmetric state, rather than where Λ(3)=0\Lambda(3) = 0, and called the oscillation self-sustaining without external drive, where the pair draws its power from the standing sound wave. Uniform beads are no longer said to confirm the role of structured asymmetry: the source finds that identical beads interact reciprocally and form no active state, which the framework reads as a correspondence of structure, and falsification criterion F3, printed as confirmed, is graded so. A physical result is read, as the theory registration reads it, as a test of the framework’s scope that proves no registered law, where the paper called it direct evidence that the alignment scaling problem is physics and physical validation of the ARC equation. The photonic time crystal of Raskatla and colleagues (2024) is described, and its title given, as published. Which form the framework states for this system’s growth from rest waits for the author’s statement; Section 5.4 says so, and the next version brings that subsection to it in one pass.

  • The March 2026 run (v5). It is described as one unregistered run of six frontier models that added a bundle of blinding steps, each response scored by five or six distinct judges depending on the subject run (six or seven seats, one judge seated twice, where the paper said six or seven scorers), never as scored blind, mutually blind or conducted under four-layer blinding, and its three tiers carry the finding of an internal code review in October 2026: for the three models that read flat or negative, the scoring endpoint’s output cap cut the deepest paraphrases before the judges saw them, and judges scored paraphrases written by their own model. Its holdout prompts are no longer called sealed, and the benchmark is no longer called the most rigorous published. Its contrasts are no longer said to confirm the prediction, or to show three models with an alignment exponent at or below zero; the measurement-scope note of 19 September 2026 states why. Its counts are given as its records give them: 28 prompts issued under the alignment task type, of the battery’s 36, and 2,170 responses, where the paper said 36 prompts and about 2,200 entries.

  • The comparison with the earlier experiment (v4). The unblinded rises for DeepSeek V3.2 and Gemini that did not hold in v5 are no longer called a complete reversal, artefacts of scorer bias or a demonstration that unblinded evaluation is wrong: DeepSeek V3.2’s association became null, Gemini’s became significantly negative on a later model, the later run changed several things together, and no single cause is claimed. Gemini’s v4 association is given as ρ=+0.275\rho = +0.275 (version 1.21: +0.311+0.311, as the run’s archived analysis record stores it) from an earlier Gemini model, the value in Paper IV.d’s table, where it was printed as +0.311+0.311 and its model as Gemini 3 Flash; the field-wide sentences are stated on the condition Paper XII’s test sets, with the earlier studies of model judges named.

  • Paper II’s numbers. The early estimate of about 2.24 is stated as retracted wherever it is printed; the best surviving estimate is given as about 0.49 by regression, with the endpoint estimate, 0.59, to which the interval −1.3-1.3 to 2.92.9 belongs, one model’s fit and inconclusive, where the interval stood beside 0.49 and the figure was called sub-linear, measured, the six-model experiment’s defensible estimate or its correction. The parallel exponents are given as Paper II’s corrections of 21 October 2026 give them: near zero in DeepSeek R1 and GPT-5.4, 0.31 in Gemini 3 Flash, 0.22 in Groq Qwen3 over all 30 problems, and none for Grok 4.1 Fast, at 100% at every sample count, where they were printed as near zero in four of the five models and as the strongest finding; the sequential exponent is said to exceed the parallel one wherever both could be estimated, where the paper said it did so robustly across all six frontier models. Grok 4.1 Fast’s tier-2 accuracy is given as 96.3% to 100%, GPT-5.4’s as 53.7% with reasoning set to none, and Groq Qwen3’s as 44.4% to 53.7%.

  • Laws IV and V, and P19. The laws are stated as registered on 15 October 2026 by version 1.103 of the theory registration, with Law IV not yet tested and Law V under test (Section 10.7), their mathematics at version 1.1, where the reading key and the epistemic-status note said the laws themselves were not yet registered and cited the mathematics at version 1.0. The opening of Section 1 now states what each of the four programmes reported, where it said each found capability gains exceeding linear accumulation; the geometric scaling bound is stated for systems whose growth runs through a supply network of finite dimension, with prokaryote metabolism and urban innovation named as systems outside that class that exceed one; the computation a brain or a machine performs is stated as physical, where the paper said it escapes physical space and that digital AI was the first system to break the bound; the thermodynamic-drag account the paper had already retired no longer frames its safety argument; the Eddington limit is stated as a luminosity ceiling, not a hard ceiling on accretion; the cosmological exponent of about 1.1, and the sentence citing Planck 2018 for it, are withdrawn, since no source for that exponent is given; the Friedmann matter-era value and the physics instances are called identities, where they were called confirmations; the percolation row is given with its sign; quantum error correction is graded as established physics, not a confirmed prediction; the quantum section names the limits on quantum speed-up; the speculative extension no longer says that the same amplification pattern is observable in time crystals, quantum error correction and AI reasoning; and the divergence at β→1\beta \to 1 is stated, as the paper’s own derivation note states it, as a divergence of the exponent, the solution tending to the exponential.

The bound is argued from the O(N2)O(N^2) cost of self-attention, not proven, for attention-based architectures, where Sections 4.5 and 10.3 and Table 27 called it proven there. It stands among the claims that need empirical validation, as the conjectured value of Law III, the ARC Ceiling, a law under test. The logical error rate is written εd∝Λ−(d+1)/2\varepsilon_d \propto \Lambda^{-(d+1)/2}, with Λ\Lambda the suppression for each increase of two in code distance, as the Willow paper and equation (9) give it, where seven places wrote Λ−d\Lambda^{-d} or Λd\Lambda^{d}, and a dated note beside Corollary 1, which keeps its words, corrects the eighth; the unit of recursive depth in quantum error correction is one step of two in code distance, where two places called it one code-distance increment or layer.
